intent_record.intent_summary: Add validation function to enforce correct port range configuration and prevent invalid range processing in multiport matching.
intent_record.what: Added a new static function `multiport_valid_ranges()` that validates port ranges in a multiport match structure by iterating through ports, checking that range flags are properly paired and that port values are in ascending order.
intent_record.how: This function enables validation of multiport configuration data before it is used in matching operations. It checks three conditions: (1) range flags must alternate (not consecutive), (2) range pairs must be complete (flag followed by another port), and (3) port values in a range must be ordered correctly (start <= end). This prevents invalid range configurations from being processed.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing port range validation to multiport_mt_check() by introducing a call to multiport_valid_ranges() after the existing protocol/invflags/count checks.
intent_record.what: Replaced a ternary operator return statement with an explicit if-check for the initial validation, and added a new call to multiport_valid_ranges() with its own ternary return statement.
intent_record.how: The function now performs two sequential validation checks instead of one. First, it validates protocol, invflags, and count via the existing check() function. If that fails, it returns -EINVAL immediately. If it passes, it then validates port ranges via the new multiport_valid_ranges() function. Previously, only the first validation was performed. This adds an additional validation step that was missing.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add missing validation of multiport ranges in IPv6 multiport match checking to prevent invalid range configurations from being accepted.
intent_record.what: Refactored the return statement in multiport_mt6_check() from a ternary expression into an if-statement with explicit error handling, and added a new validation call to multiport_valid_ranges(multiinfo) before the final return.
intent_record.how: The function now performs two sequential validation checks instead of one: first it validates the protocol/flags/count via check(), and if that passes, it additionally validates the port ranges via multiport_valid_ranges(). Previously, only the first check was performed. The function will now return -EINVAL if either validation fails, providing more comprehensive validation of multiport match parameters.

candidates.rationale: The multiport_mt_check() function only calls check() which validates protocol, invflags, and count, but does not validate the internal structure of port ranges in the pflags array. This allows malformed range encodings (range starts at last slot or consecutive range starts) to pass validation.

The multiport_mt6_check() function has the same validation gap as multiport_mt_check(). It only validates protocol, invflags, and count without checking the internal structure of port ranges in the pflags array, allowing invalid range configurations to pass.

The ports_match_v1() function is called without prior validation of the port range structure in pflags. If malformed ranges are passed (e.g., range start at last slot), this function will perform out-of-bounds access when processing the invalid range encoding.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerability exists in the checkentry validation functions (checkentry, checkentry_v1, checkentry6, checkentry6_v1) which all call the check() function. The check() function only validates basic parameters like protocol, flags, and count (line 161-167), but it does NOT validate the internal structure of the pflags array. Specifically, it fails to check: (1) that range starts (pflags[i]==1) are not at the last slot (count-1), which would cause out-of-bounds access when ports_match_v1() does ++i at line 62, and (2) that consecutive range starts don't occur. The ports_match_v1() function at line 62 performs 'e = minfo->ports[++i]' without bounds checking when minfo->pflags[i] is set, assuming the checkentry validation has ensured valid range encoding. Since checkentry_v1 (line 189-198) only calls check() which lacks pflags validation, malformed rules with range starts at the last slot or consecutive range starts can pass validation and later cause out-of-bounds access in ports_match_v1().
